Mostly public cloud; they want Redwood hosted API for fast time-to-value. Key ask: robust handling of 429s and short-term traffic spikes (Black Friday-like micro peaks from marketing blasts). Will likely convert to paid once burst handling is validated and pricing for burst buffer is clear.

Traffic profile & constraints (from engineering): baseline 80-120 reqs/sec during business hours, short bursts to 900-1400 reqs/sec for 3-12 minutes after campaign pushes. Median tokens/request ~420, tail up to ~1.5k tokens for longer context. Desired latency target: p95 < 500ms for generation calls; cost sensitivity high — wants cost per convo below $0.02 on average.

Specific asks from call: "How do you surface per-route quotas vs org-level?", "Can Redwood provide a short burst allowance that won't immediately 429 us on first big spike?" They requested recommended client strategy: token-based throttling, concurrency cap per worker, and graceful 429 handling with Retry-After guidance.

POC idea: create sandbox org with a temporary increased burst window for two weeks, run synthetic spike tests (we can provide load harness). Metrics to validate: 429 rate (target <0.5% during peaks), p95 latency, tokens/sec cost.

Sales notes: good conversion potential for Hosted API (self-serve -> low-touch). Not enterprise procurement; legal review only if we propose long-term committed burst buffer. Priorities: clear docs on quotas, example SDK backoff + client-side queues, transparent pricing for burst consumption.

Quotes / snippets from product lead: "We need to survive marketing spikes without shipping a costly overprovisioned architecture."
